summary: Trust boundary is CLI argv (src/playtest/cli.ts). --game is an exact-match enum ('SNG' rejected). --stacks uses an anchored, linear regex ^[0-9]+(,[0-9]+)*$ (no ReDoS, rejects hex/sign/exponent/empty fields), checks length === size, each value <= MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (a value like 9007199254740993 rounds to 2^53 and is rejected), at least two positive seats, and float total <= MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (an overflowing true sum rounds to >= 2^53, so it is rejected). The button must be a seat with chips; --stacks without --replay-code is rejected. Error messages do not echo the bad value; the echoed Options/Replay line uses the normalized numeric stacks only. Engine floor (src/engine/hand.ts) now requires isPositiveSafeInteger per stack plus the existing total bound, so createHand still fails closed on bad programmatic input; blinds post min(blind, stack) so no negative stacks, and chips posted (added) are recorded separately from the blind size. Runner carry-over derives stacks from engine final state (conserved) and checkDeal adds a cross-hand chip check. Probed live: stacks 9007199254740990,1 and 1,0,0,0,0,9007199254740990 play cleanly with no invariant violations; 1,1,1,1,1,1 sng and 1..6 sng play cleanly; out-of-range/overflowing/hex inputs exit 2. Fixed-limit betting caps actions per hand, so huge stacks add no work; --hands keeps its existing 1e9 cap. Replay-code word 2 (0 cash / 1 sng) is a constant from an enum, not attacker-controlled. No new dependencies, secrets, network, file I/O or randomness sources. No findings.
